answer: The raven multiplier is published, charged in marble, and cipher lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 2 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3268 identities would post 2381 proofs and burn roughly 2 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
